macro_blurb: US equities are being driven by sharp single-stock moves on earnings: a 31% jump in Dell on its fastest server sales growth since its 2018 relisting and an 8% gain in Okta on agentic AI demand highlight ongoing enthusiasm for AI infrastructure and cybersecurity, while Gap fell 14% after cutting sales guidance on weak Old Navy performance, underscoring divergence within US consumer retail also visible in American Eagle's strong Aerie versus its lagging namesake brand. The US consumer backdrop is softening, with the household savings rate dropping to its lowest since 2022 as inflation outpaces wages, even as Costco flagged record gasoline volumes amid rising fuel prices. On the regulatory front, Disney's ABC filed broadcast license renewals "under protest" against the FCC, keeping US media-policy risk in focus.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a value-and-yield slate dressed up with momentum: average Value sits at the 87th percentile, Yield at 83rd, Momentum at 86th, while Quality lags at 54. All 10 picks are US-listed — zero European representation despite the broad universe — and the sector spread is genuinely diffuse: Consumer Defensive, Industrials and Healthcare each get two seats, with Technology, Energy, Basic Materials and Consumer Cyclical splitting the rest. The composite range is tight (75.4 to 86.5), so no single name dominates. The dominant signal is cheapness that the market has already started to reprice — eight of ten names show positive 3-month returns against negative sector medians.

The clearest thread runs through the high-yield value names hitched to deteriorating fundamentals: MO, KHC and BBY all clear the 85th percentile on Yield (5.88%, 6.56%, 5.95%) at single-digit-to-mid-teen P/Es, but KHC's ROE is -12.6% and BBY's price-to-book sits at 5.3x. Against a softening US consumer — savings rate at a 2022 low, Gap down 14% on guidance — these dividends are the thesis and the risk. Separately, DAL, DVA and MAS all carry sector-anomalous leverage (D/E of 105, 1,261, 12,229) that the Value score doesn't penalize.

The outlier is HPQ — the only Tech name, top-2% Value, but flagged for trimmed guidance on memory costs, sitting awkwardly against the Dell/Okta AI-infrastructure tape rather than riding it. The conspicuous absence: Financial Services, Utilities, Real Estate and Communication Services produced nothing — striking given rate-sensitive yield plays usually surface here. Watch two things over the next fortnight: further US consumer data feeding through to MO, KHC and BBY, and any oil move on US-Iran headlines, which would hit APA's leveraged setup first.
